cues: Oxidation needs a hydrogen on the alpha carbon.
A primary alcohol has two, so it goes to an aldehyde and then on to a carboxylic acid, unless the volatile aldehyde is distilled off as it forms.
A secondary alcohol has one, so it stops at a ketone.
A tertiary alcohol has none, and resists mild oxidation.
